correctness.rationale: Real symmetric factors admit separate orthogonal diagonalization. Every error eigenvalue is \(\operatorname{Cov}(e^{-aT},e^{-bT})\) for \(T\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), giving positivity and strictness. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds it by \(\max_{t>0}W(t)\), attained when \(a=b\). The derivative numerator has one positive zero: \(H\'\'\'(t)=-4e^tJ(t)\), \(J\'\'(t)=(2t-1)e^t\), and derivative sign propagation from the zero initial conditions proves uniqueness. Exact-rational Taylor remainder enclosures certify the numerical bracket and sharp constant. The standalone verifier runs 51,545 assertions; grids do not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The published direction split evaluates Kronecker-sum matrix exponential integrals efficiently. The sharp absolute norm-error ceiling \(C_*=0.066139893975\ldots\), its attaining spectral geometry, positive-semidefinite sign, and arbitrarily poor relative retention quantify a natural stiffness-dependent accuracy limit absent from the fixed-generator \(O(h^2)\) statement. This directly motivates reliable numerical error budgeting, without claiming a full-scheme convergence result.
